chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa said: He narrated to me Ali ibn Bilal, and it seemed to me that I had heard it from Ali ibn Bilal, who said:

I wrote to him: Is it permissible for a man to be in one town and another man, one of his brothers, in another town, who needs him, to pay the Fitrah to him or not? So he wrote: He distributes the Fitrah among those who are present in that town and does not send it to another town, even if he does not find a suitable recipient there.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitrah, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Where should Fitrah be distributed: locally or can it be sent elsewhere?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Ali ibn Bilal conveys Imam al-Sadiq's ruling that Fitrah is primarily a local obligation, to be distributed among the poor residing in the same town as the payer. This establishes the principle of prioritizing immediate community needs over remote distribution, a view supported by Shia jurists who emphasize the social cohesion aspect of Zakat al-Fitr. The exception for sending it elsewhere applies only when no suitable recipients are available locally, highlighting the pragmatic flexibility within the strict local mandate.
